# Creative MCP

> Creative MCP is an open collection of local Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that connect AI agents and MCP clients to creative software: Adobe MCP for InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, After Effects and Premiere Pro, and Blender MCP for Blender. Servers run on the user's own machine over stdio; nothing is hosted.

Key facts:
- Adobe MCP: five app-specific Node.js servers (Node.js 18+, macOS or Windows) plus a Suite coordinator for two documented Illustrator-to-InDesign workflows. npm: `adobe-mcp-suite`. Homebrew: `brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp` (v0.3.0). Source: https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp (MIT).
- Blender MCP: a Rust MCP server and CLI with a companion Blender add-on (Blender 4.0+); `blender-mcp addon install` installs and turns on the add-on. Homebrew: `brew install zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp` (v0.5.1). Source: https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs (MIT OR Apache-2.0).
- The projects are independent. A client can load both, but moving files between Adobe apps and Blender is a user-managed handoff.
- Capability status is reported as Documented, Implemented, Tested or Validated; those levels are distinct and a lower level never implies a higher one.
- Created by Zach Shallbetter (https://zachshallbetter.com/).
- Website, docs and the series catalogue (https://creativemcp.com/registry.json) are open source at https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp.
- Each tool has its own repository and release cycle; they share the Homebrew tap `zachshallbetter/tap`. One installer sets up the series: `brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp` then `creative-mcp setup` (detects apps and MCP clients, installs, registers only what is missing, verifies; safe to rerun; macOS fully supported). `creative-mcp doctor` checks servers, running apps and client registrations; `creative-mcp update` and `creative-mcp remove` handle the rest. The installer is built from the catalogue.

---

Source: https://creativemcp.com/

## One protocol. Different creative worlds.

Creative MCP hosts independent, open implementations that connect creative tools to agent workflows.

[### Adobe MCP

Connect your Adobe creative apps.
Available

Five app-specific MCP servers, with a coordinator for supported cross-app workflows.
Explore Adobe MCP ↗](https://creativemcp.com/apps.html) [### Blender MCP

Work with 3D scenes, objects, materials and animation.
Available

A Rust MCP server and Blender companion add-on for scene tools, assets and pipelines.
Explore Blender MCP ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)

＋ More creative tools can join as they’re ready.

Creative MCP is an open platform; implementations are developed and released independently.

How it works

## Get from idea to output in three steps.

A simple local setup connects your creative applications to your chosen agent workflow.

### Choose a tool

Pick an implementation, such as Adobe MCP or Blender MCP.

### Connect your MCP client

Install and configure the local server and any app companion it needs.

### Keep creating in your app

Your tools stay open on your machine. Work with your files and context where supported.

[See setup details and implementation requirements →](https://creativemcp.com/how-it-works.html)

Built for real work

Capability & evidence

## Clear signals for what’s ready.

Each implementation provides transparent information about its current capabilities, so you know what to expect.

Documented

Guides explain what the implementation does and how to set it up.

Implemented

The tools and capabilities are present in the MCP server.

Tested

Automated checks cover the tool implementation where provided.

Validated

Live-app validation is reported separately and depends on the implementation.

Adobe MCP’s [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html) tracks evidence by feature. For Blender MCP, see the project’s current repository documentation. A tool passing automated checks does not by itself prove that a workflow has been validated in a live application.

Beyond one app

## From layout to a 3D scene.

Move approved artwork and its context into Blender, then keep building in the tools you already use.

01 / 03

### Design the composition

Shape a layout and approve the artwork in InDesign.

02 / 03

### Move the working files

Export the approved assets and carry the brief into the next tool.

03 / 03

### Develop the scene

Bring those assets into Blender and continue building in 3D.

How the handoff worksThis is a file handoff between separate MCP implementations. Direct Adobe-to-Blender orchestration is not currently provided. [Explore the workflow gallery →](https://creativemcp.com/workflows.html)

Open implementations · local creative tools

# One protocol. Different creative worlds.

Creative MCP brings together independent implementations for the creative applications you already use. Each project has its own setup, requirements and capabilities.

## Implementations

### Adobe MCP

Local MCP servers for InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, After Effects and Premiere Pro, with a coordinator for two documented cross-app workflows.

- Five application-specific implementations
- One suite coordinator for two documented cross-app workflows
- Node.js 18+, macOS or Windows
- Install with `brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp` or npx
[Explore Adobe MCP →](https://creativemcp.com/apps.html)

### Blender MCP

A Rust MCP server and companion Blender add-on for scenes, objects, materials and 3D asset pipelines.

- Stdio MCP server with local Blender IPC
- Blender 4.0+ and the companion add-on
- Install with `brew install zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp` or Cargo from source
[Explore Blender MCP →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)

These projects are separate MCP implementations. They can be configured in a compatible client at the same time, but direct Adobe-to-Blender orchestration is not currently part of either project.

Adobe MCP · five creative surfaces

## Choose a place to start.

Each Adobe server has its own tools and workflow. Read the implementation guide for app-specific requirements and behavior.

[Browse Adobe application implementations →](https://creativemcp.com/apps.html) · [Explore the Capability Atlas →](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html)

Local setup · your tools stay yours

# Get from idea to output in three steps.

An MCP client starts a local server for the creative implementation you choose. That server connects to its supported application, so an agent can use the tools and context the implementation exposes.

## The three steps

### Choose an implementation

Start with Adobe MCP for Adobe apps or Blender MCP for 3D work. Check each project’s prerequisites and supported workflows.

### Connect your MCP client

Install the implementation and add its local launch command to a compatible client. Some projects also require an app-side companion add-on.

### Keep creating in your app

Open the creative application and let your client use the available tools against local work, files and context.

Choose your path

## Each project has its own setup.

### Adobe MCP

Install the Suite coordinator or an app-specific server. It runs with Node.js and connects to the Adobe desktop application on the same machine.

```
claude mcp add --scope user adobe -- npx -y adobe-mcp-suite
```

Or install every Adobe server with Homebrew:

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
```

[Adobe setup guide →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)

### Blender MCP

Install the Rust CLI and its Blender companion add-on. The add-on must be enabled in Blender 4.0 or later.

```
cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs --package blender-mcp-cli
```

Or let Homebrew build it for you:

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp
```

[Blender setup guide →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)

One client · local implementations

## Follow the work from prompt to app.

The client communicates with each server over MCP. Implementations reach their target applications using the app-specific route documented by that project.

Capability & evidence

## Know what a status means.

Documented

Project guides describe the behavior and requirements.

Implemented

The capability is present in that implementation’s tools.

Tested

Automated checks cover the code or tool behavior they target.

Validated

The workflow has been run in the actual application and its result checked. This state is tracked separately.

Adobe MCP publishes feature-level research and evidence in its [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html). Validation depends on the specific application and workflow; automated checks alone do not prove live-app behavior.

Project boundaries

## Separate tools. Clear handoffs.

Adobe MCP and Blender MCP are independent projects. A compatible client can expose both to the same workflow, but moving a file between them is currently a user-managed handoff rather than a direct cross-project tool.

[Explore projects →](https://creativemcp.com/projects.html) · [Browse workflow examples →](https://creativemcp.com/workflows.html) · [Browse documentation →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)

The person behind Creative MCP

# An artist who builds creative software.

Zach Shallbetter is an artist, designer, and creative technologist based in Spokane, Washington. He founded Snack Studio and created Creative MCP. It brings his Adobe MCP and Blender MCP projects together. The tools connect AI agents with creative software.
Meet Zach

[Image: Illustrated portrait of Zach Shallbetter seated in a vivid, paint-filled creative studio]

Zach Shallbetter · artist, designer, creative technologist

Why Creative MCP exists

## Creative work deserves tools that understand the work.

Creative MCP connects AI agents to the software used by artists and designers. Each implementation gives an MCP client a local path into a creative tool. Instructions and context can meet real documents, artwork, scenes, and timelines.

The aim is practical: make creative software easier to reach through conversation and code. The application and its files stay in the workflow. So does the creator’s judgment.

What makes it different

## Built for creative practice. Clear about its limits.

01

### Close to the work

Local MCP servers connect agents with supported desktop applications and the work already open there.

02

### Made for distinct tools

InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, After Effects, Premiere Pro, and Blender each have different creative surfaces and implementation needs.

03

### Evidence stays visible

The Adobe Capability Atlas separates documented features, automation routes, implementation coverage, checks, and live-app validation.

[Explore the implementations →](https://creativemcp.com/projects.html)[Read the Capability Atlas →](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html)[Browse the documentation →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)

A practice across art and technology

## Drawing led to creative technology.

Zach’s practice began with drawing, illustration, comics, and murals. It grew into interface design, interactive media, and creative production software.

For more than twenty years, he has worked between visual storytelling and technical implementation. Recent projects include computer-vision tools for video production. They support rotoscoping, object callouts, and masking. His [InDesign MCP server exposes 137 tools](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/indesign).

Creative MCP extends that work across Adobe applications and Blender. It connects code and conversation to the tools artists and designers use.

About the creator

## Zach Shallbetter

Zach approaches creative software as an artist who builds his own tools. He wants creators to express an idea, shape the result, and understand what their tools are doing.

Artist · Designer · Creative technologist · Spokane, Washington

Field guide · setup to first workflow

# Get set up.

Install the local servers, connect them to your MCP client, understand which Adobe app each package reaches, and troubleshoot the bridge between your model and your creative work.

LOCAL PROCESS · MCP OVER STDIO · macOS + WINDOWS

On this page [Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Content guide](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)How it worksChoose a packageRequirements Quick startMCP client setupSuite coordinator App setupFirst workflowsConfiguration Files & safetyTroubleshootingReference library

## How it works

These are desktop automation servers. Your MCP client starts a Node.js process on the same computer as the Adobe app. The server accepts MCP messages over standard input/output (stdio), translates a tool call into an application script or bridge request, and returns the result to the client.

01 · Ask

### Your MCP client

Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Warp, or another client that can launch an MCP server process.

02 · Route

### Local MCP server

Node runs on your machine. The server validates arguments and routes the request to the selected application backend.

03 · Act

### Adobe desktop app

The app must be installed and generally open (or launchable). Your client and Adobe files stay in your local workflow.

Not a hosted Adobe endpoint. The public website provides documentation and the capability atlas. Tool execution happens locally through the server process you configure in your MCP client; this website does not proxy MCP calls.

## Choose a package

Install one app server for direct control of that application. Add the Suite coordinator when you want its current cross-app workflows. The coordinator does not expose the full tool list of its child servers.

| Package | Use it for | Connection route | Install

| InDesign
`adobe-mcp-indesign` | Documents, pages, typography, tables, long documents and export. | ExtendScript via AppleScript on macOS or COM/PowerShell on Windows; optional UXP backend. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-indesign`

| Illustrator
`adobe-mcp-illustrator` | Documents, artboards, layers, vectors, typography, effects and export. | ExtendScript via AppleScript on macOS or COM/PowerShell on Windows. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-illustrator`

| Photoshop
`adobe-mcp-photoshop` | Documents, pixels, layers, selections, adjustments, painting and export. | ExtendScript through local desktop automation. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-photoshop`

| After Effects
`adobe-mcp-aftereffects` | Projects, footage, compositions, layers, keyframes, effects and render queue. | ExtendScript through local desktop automation. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-aftereffects`

| Premiere Pro
`adobe-mcp-premiere` | Projects, sequences, timeline edits, markers, effects and export. | Local WebSocket bridge to a UXP plugin panel in Premiere Pro. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-premiere`

| Suite coordinator
`adobe-mcp-suite` | Two coordinated Illustrator → InDesign handoffs. | Starts child MCP servers locally and delegates workflow steps. | `npx -y adobe-mcp-suite`

Tool counts, exact coverage, evidence levels and known gaps are in the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html). The individual package guides document each package's current tool surfaces and options.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later. Use an up-to-date LTS release; `npx` ships with npm.
- macOS or Windows for the listed desktop server integrations. macOS may prompt you to authorize Terminal or Node to control an Adobe app in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.
- The corresponding Adobe desktop app installed on the same computer. InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects guides specify 2023+; Premiere Pro requires 25.6+ and its MCP Bridge UXP plugin loaded.
- An MCP client that can launch a command with arguments and environment variables and communicate over stdio.
- Premiere only: UXP Developer Tool to load the plugin until a published installation path is documented; plugin/server ports and bridge token must match.

Adobe app versions and backend support can differ by operation. Consult the app guide and the tool's `help` response for version-specific behavior.

## Quick start

The fastest path on a Mac: the `creative-mcp` installer finds your Adobe apps, Blender and MCP clients, and sets everything up after showing you the plan.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp
creative-mcp setup
```

It ends by naming the clients to restart and a few requests to try. From then on, `creative-mcp doctor` checks the servers, the open apps and every client's registrations, and `creative-mcp update` keeps everything current. See [all installer commands](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html#installer).

To set things up by hand instead:

- Install Node.js 18 or later and the Adobe application you intend to automate.
- Register the matching package in your MCP client using the setup below.
- Restart or reconnect the MCP client so it launches the process and refreshes its tool list.
- Open the Adobe app and a suitable document (or ask a read-only status tool what is open).
- Start with a small, reversible request. Confirm the target document, selection, units and output path before asking for a change or export.

For example: “In the active Illustrator document, list the artboards and report their sizes. Don’t make changes.” Once the connection is confirmed, try a bounded edit in a copy of a document.

## MCP client setup

### Claude Code: one app server

```
claude mcp add --scope user illustrator -- npx -y adobe-mcp-illustrator
```

Replace `illustrator` and the package name with the Adobe application you want. Omit `--scope user` if you prefer the client’s default scope.

### Claude Code: the Suite coordinator

```
claude mcp add --scope user adobe -- npx -y adobe-mcp-suite
```

### Any client with an `mcpServers` configuration

```
{
"mcpServers": {
"illustrator": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "adobe-mcp-illustrator"]
}
}
}
```

For Claude Desktop, edit its MCP server configuration file. Cursor, Warp and other clients use their own configuration screen or file; follow the client’s current instructions for where to place this block. Do not paste the JSON into a shell command. See the dedicated [CLI and configuration reference](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html) for source-checkout launch and environment-variable details.

### Run a specific published version

```
{
"mcpServers": {
"illustrator": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "adobe-mcp-illustrator@0.9.0"]
}
}
}
```

Pin the package version when you need repeatable team setups; check npm for the current published version before updating the pin.

### Install with Homebrew

On macOS or Linux, the Creative MCP tap installs the Suite coordinator and every app server onto your `PATH`, so clients can launch them without `npx`. Homebrew 7 and later asks you to trust a third-party tap once.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
claude mcp add adobe -- adobe-mcp-suite
claude mcp add illustrator -- adobe-mcp-illustrator
```

## Suite coordinator

The coordinator currently offers two workflows across InDesign and Illustrator. It starts the app servers it needs as child MCP processes, then delegates the individual actions. Install an app's standalone package as well if you need its direct tools in your client.

Illustrator → InDesign

### Place artwork

Place an artboard from the active Illustrator document on an InDesign page as a link to its `.ai` source. The Illustrator document is saved first by default.

Illustrator → InDesign

### Copy swatches

Copy supported process and spot swatches with exact values. Gradients and patterns are reported, not copied; built-in InDesign swatches are preserved.

### Select which child servers load

```
npx -y adobe-mcp-suite --apps indesign,illustrator
# or set ADOBE_MCP_APPS=indesign,illustrator
```

The supported app IDs are `indesign`, `illustrator`, `photoshop`, `aftereffects` and `premiere`. The current coordinator workflows require both InDesign and Illustrator. Selecting other apps does not add new cross-app workflows or re-export their tools.

### Allow the files needed by a workflow

File operations are confined to the user’s home directory and any additional per-app allowed directories. For a handoff, configure both participating servers for the directory containing the source artwork and the destination document as needed.

```
{
"mcpServers": {
"adobe": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "adobe-mcp-suite", "--apps", "indesign,illustrator"],
"env": {
"INDESIGN_ALLOWED_DIRS": "/Users/you/Projects",
"ILLUSTRATOR_ALLOWED_DIRS": "/Users/you/Projects"
}
}
}
}
```

On Windows, use a Windows path and separate multiple allowed directories with semicolons. The coordinator forwards each server only the variables it needs.

## Application setup

Each app server has its own behavior, terminology, tool names and supported operations. Its MCP `help` tool describes parameters and categories from the definitions the server advertises.

Desktop automation

### InDesign

macOS uses AppleScript; Windows uses COM via PowerShell. Optional UXP bridge support is available. The guide explains page units, document selection, path permissions and backend selection.

[Read the InDesign guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)

Desktop automation

### Illustrator

Learn artboard-relative geometry, coordinate direction, item targeting, color formats, fonts and allowed paths before editing artwork.

[Read the Illustrator guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)

Desktop automation

### Photoshop

Review layer and selection identifiers, image dimensions, file operations, export options and its local target/backend settings.

[Read the Photoshop guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)

Desktop automation

### After Effects

Review composition and layer targeting, time/keyframe conventions, render queue behavior, file access and script timeout settings.

[Read the After Effects guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)

UXP plugin bridge

### Premiere Pro

Load the MCP Bridge panel, match its port and optional token to the server, and understand its tested status and API-version limits.

[Read the Premiere Pro guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)

Premiere Pro validation status: the repository guide says the server has not yet been tested against a real Premiere Pro session. Script checks and a stand-in test DOM do not establish live-app validation. See the guide’s “What is not certain yet” section.

## Plan a first workflow

- Inspect before editing. Ask for app status, document/project information, selections and relevant items first.
- Specify the target. Name the active document or use stable IDs returned by list tools. Avoid relying on a repeated display name when IDs are available.
- State units and bounds. Provide page/artboard dimensions, pixel sizes, frame/time units and a bounded set of objects where the tool requires them.
- Choose an output path. Use a path in your home folder or explicitly allowed directory. Do not overwrite an existing deliverable unless you intend to.
- Review before destructive work. Duplicate the document or project, check the intended selection, and ask the client to confirm before deleting, closing without saving, or replacing output.
- Verify in the Adobe app. Open or inspect the result, check links/fonts/render status as appropriate, and save/export deliberately.

Tool calls are discrete operations. A sequence of calls is not automatically an all-or-nothing transaction; inspect intermediate state when the workflow depends on a prior change.

## Configuration

Set environment variables in the MCP client’s server entry. Do not set them in a website form or commit real credentials to a repository.

| Variable family | Applies to | Purpose

| `*_ALLOWED_DIRS` | Each app server, e.g. `PHOTOSHOP_ALLOWED_DIRS` | Add directories to the default home-folder file access scope. Delimiter is platform-specific: `:` on macOS, `;` on Windows.

| `ADOBE_MCP_APPS` | Suite coordinator | Choose which app server IDs the coordinator starts.

| `*_APP_NAME` | App-specific, where supported | Select a local Adobe application installation. Availability and behavior vary by package and operating system.

| `*_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS` | App-specific | Adjust how long a server waits for a script or bridge response. See the package guide for defaults and exceptions.

| `*_TARGET`, `ADOBE_TARGET` | Supported ArtCraft-compatible servers | Route compatible operations to a named local ArtCraft adapter. Support is app-specific; consult that server’s guide.

| `PREMIERE_WS_PORT` | Premiere Pro | Choose the loopback port used by the local server and set the same port in the UXP bridge panel.

| `BRIDGE_TOKEN`, `PREMIERE_BRIDGE_TOKEN` | Premiere Pro | Optional local bridge authentication; use the per-server override when coordinating with another bridge consumer. Keep tokens private.

| `UXP_BRIDGE_URL` | Packages with a UXP backend | Set the local bridge address only where the app guide documents that backend.

Variable names do not imply every package supports every option. Confirm the exact variable, default, delimiter and forwarding behavior in the package README.

## Files, permissions & safety

- Local process, local authority. MCP tools can make changes in the desktop application under your user session. Grant only the client permissions needed for the apps you use.
- File paths are constrained. Shared path policy confines supported file operations to the home directory and configured allowed directories, and rejects system-directory paths. An app may still interpret its own document references according to its own behavior.
- Destructive operations need review. Deleting pages/layers/clips, closing unsaved work, replacing files and similar actions can lose work. Tool annotations help capable clients recognize destructive or open-world calls; review each target and result.
- Use copies for consequential edits. Save a working copy, inspect the active document/selection and verify output before relying on an automated result.
- Premiere bridge stays local. Its documented server binds to loopback. A bridge token is stored by the plugin panel in local storage; protect access to the machine and do not share the token.
- Custom code is powerful. App-specific execution tools that accept code are not equivalent to ordinary constrained editing tools. Read their package security notes before enabling or using them.

## Troubleshooting

### The server does not appear in the client

Check the client’s MCP configuration syntax, command name and package spelling. Confirm Node/npm are on the client process PATH, then restart or reconnect the client and inspect its MCP logs.

### The client cannot start `npx`

Run `node --version` and `npm --version` in a terminal. Install Node.js 18+ and ensure the client app inherits a PATH that includes Node and npm.

### The server says no document is open

Open the target Adobe app and a document/project. Ask for the app’s status or list tools first, then identify the intended active document.

### macOS asks for Automation permission

Approve the prompt for the process actually controlling the Adobe app (often Terminal, the MCP client, or Node). Review it under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

### A file path is rejected

Use an absolute path inside your home directory or add its parent directory to that server’s `*_ALLOWED_DIRS`. Restart the MCP server after changing client environment settings.

### Premiere says the bridge is disconnected

Confirm Premiere Pro 25.6+, load the UXP plugin and open its MCP Bridge panel. Match its port and token to the server configuration; then run `premiere_status`.

### A call times out

Check for a modal dialog in the Adobe app and verify the app is responsive. Some renders and long operations need a longer package-specific timeout; do not blindly retry an operation that may have completed.

### A tool or parameter is unfamiliar

Call `help` for a tool or category. Use the exact advertised argument names and inspect current document state rather than guessing IDs or enum values.

### A cross-app workflow is missing

The coordinator currently advertises its supported InDesign/Illustrator workflows only when both child servers are loaded. It does not expose standalone app tools.

## Reference library

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / Content & capability guide

What the tools work on

# Content & capability guide

Understand the difference between an Adobe feature, an automation route, an MCP implementation, a passing static check, and a workflow verified in the live application.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## Six different things called “coverage”

| Stage | What it means | What it does not establish

| Documented | A feature appears in Adobe product guides, scripting references or other cited source material. | That an API can reach it or an MCP server has a tool for it.

| Scriptable | A known automation route may reach the feature: object model, menu command, UXP API or another documented route. | That the route is supported on every OS/app version or covered by this project.

| Implemented | An MCP tool is mapped to the feature in the atlas dataset. | That the mapping is complete, the app accepted the operation, or the result is correct.

| Static checks | Generated scripts were exercised with a stubbed application and checked against the relevant API/type information. | Live behavior, application version compatibility, visual quality or successful production output.

| Live validated | A workflow was run in the actual Adobe app and its result checked. | Universal behavior beyond the tested version, document, platform and conditions.

Atlas percentages use that app’s documented feature count as the denominator. Tool counts represent MCP tools mapped in that dataset. Read the snapshot date and methodology before comparing releases.

## What the app servers work on

### InDesign

Documents and books, pages and spreads, text, tables, styles, color, images, long-document structure, interactive output, prepress and export.

### Illustrator

Documents, artboards, layers, vector shapes and paths, text, swatches, appearance, effects, symbols, data sets, images, actions and output.

### Photoshop

Documents and canvas, pixels, layers and masks, selections, channels, adjustments, filters, painting, retouching, type, actions and export.

### After Effects

Projects and footage, compositions, layers and time, keyframes, expressions, effects, text, masks, shapes, tracking, 3D and rendering.

### Premiere Pro

Projects and media, sequences, timeline edits, markers, effects, keyframes, color, audio, captions/transcripts, metadata and export.

### Suite coordinator

Two explicitly coordinated workflows today: place Illustrator artwork in InDesign and copy supported swatches from Illustrator to InDesign.

Use the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html) to explore the detailed feature inventory and its sources. Use each [implementation guide](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) for tool behavior and package-specific constraints.

## Choose by content

- Read before write: request status, document/project information, list results and selected items before making edits.
- Stable target: use IDs returned by list/create tools where the app supports them; verify the selection and active document.
- App-native units: follow the specific app guide. InDesign documentation commonly specifies millimetres; Illustrator uses points from an artboard’s top-left with y increasing downward; Photoshop geometry is pixels from the document top-left; Premiere time values are seconds.
- Export is its own workflow: specify format, preset/options, path and whether overwrite is intended; confirm the generated file in the target app or viewer.
- Coverage is not endorsement: the Atlas may document features that are inaccessible through a script route or absent from our tools.

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / MCP API reference

Protocol surface · tool schemas

# MCP API reference

The Adobe servers expose tools through MCP over stdio. Use the server’s advertised schema as the executable contract; this page explains discovery, calls, instructions, results and where to find exact per-tool parameters.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## Transport and lifecycle

The MCP client launches the configured command as a local process and communicates over standard input/output. The process stdout is protocol traffic; startup diagnostics belong on stderr. There is no public HTTP API for the desktop servers.

- The client starts the server and negotiates MCP initialization.
- The server returns its identity, capabilities and app-specific usage instructions.
- The client discovers tool names and JSON input schemas with `tools/list`.
- The client invokes a tool with `tools/call` and arguments that match the advertised schema.
- The server validates inputs, performs the app operation, then returns structured text/content or an error result.

## Discover the live API

Do not treat a marketing summary, Atlas row or old copy of a README as the current schema. The connected server’s `tools/list` is authoritative for the tool names and inputs exposed by that running package.

Discovery

### `tools/list`

Returns advertised tools and their JSON input schemas. Reconnect after a package upgrade so the client refreshes its list.

Detailed guidance

### `help`

App servers with the help utility can describe a tool, list categories, and provide detailed usage/examples. Consult the app-specific guide for its exact formats.

Execution

### `tools/call`

Calls one tool using the exact tool name and schema-defined argument object. Respect enum, unit, target and path constraints.

```
Client action (conceptual):
discover tools → choose an advertised name
call tool with arguments matching that tool's input schema
inspect isError and returned content before continuing
```

Use the package tool references for full parameter tables: [InDesign generated tool reference](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/indesign/docs), and the [Illustrator](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/illustrator), [Photoshop](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/photoshop), [After Effects](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/aftereffects), [Premiere](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/premiere) and [Suite](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/suite) READMEs.

## Tool metadata and results

- Input schema: use the exact property names, required fields, types, ranges and enum values returned by the server.
- Instructions: server instructions explain app conventions such as units, indices, colors, path rules, errors and safe targeting. MCP clients may pass them to the model as connection context.
- Annotations: supported tools may identify read-only, destructive, idempotent and open-world behavior. Treat annotations as useful metadata, not a replacement for checking the target.
- Errors: a failed tool may return `isError: true` with a message. Stop and interpret that result; do not assume the operation partially or fully succeeded.
- Stateful application: active document, selection, current sequence and UI state can change between calls. Re-read state when later steps depend on it.

Suite API is intentionally narrow. The coordinator exposes its cross-app workflows; it does not proxy every child server’s tools. Connect an app package separately for direct application tools.

## Execution boundaries

Most app tools generate a script for ExtendScript or UXP and send it to a local Adobe app or plugin. Premiere Pro uses its UXP Bridge panel. The tool call is local computer automation with the permissions of the configured process; it is not a hosted service request. Review app-specific notes about unrestricted code-execution tools before using them.

---

Source: https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / CLI & configuration

Installer · launch commands · environment

# CLI & configuration

One command, `creative-mcp`, installs the servers, registers them with your MCP clients and keeps them healthy. The servers themselves are MCP processes your client launches, not command-line utilities.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## The creative-mcp installer

Install it with Homebrew, then let it find your apps and clients:

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp
creative-mcp setup
```

Nothing to drag into an app or copy into a config file: `setup` shows its plan, asks once, installs, registers and checks. It ends by telling you which clients to restart and a few requests to try. Run it again at any time; when everything is in place it says so and changes nothing.

| Command | What it does

| `creative-mcp setup` | Detects your creative apps and MCP clients, suggests the matching tools, installs them and registers only what is missing or out of date.

| `creative-mcp doctor` | Checks every server answers, asks each running app whether it is reachable (it never starts an app), runs the Blender add-on check and shows which clients have which servers. Every problem ends with the command that fixes it.

| `creative-mcp update` | Runs `brew update`, upgrades the installed tools and creative-mcp itself, reinstalls the Blender add-on and fixes registrations that point at an old command.

| `creative-mcp add blender` | Sets up named tools even when no matching app was detected.

| `creative-mcp remove blender` | Removes the tool from every client, then uninstalls it. Add `--no-install` to keep it installed.

| `creative-mcp detect`, `list` | What was found on this machine; every tool in the catalogue and whether it is installed.

Options: `--dry-run` prints the plan and changes nothing; `--yes` accepts the suggestions without prompting; `--tools adobe,blender` and `--clients claude-code,codex,cursor` narrow the choice; `--no-install` only registers; `--json` gives machine-readable output for `detect`, `list` and `doctor`.

### How it registers servers

- Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI: through their own `mcp add` commands at user scope. When `claude` isn't on your `PATH`, it uses the Claude Code CLI that ships with Claude Desktop.
- Claude Desktop, Cursor: by adding `mcpServers` entries to their JSON config. The file is backed up once before the first change, and every other setting is kept.
- Anything else: it prints the exact entry to add.

Detection reads app bundles, `PATH` and client config files on your machine and sends nothing anywhere. Status: Implemented and tested (v0.2.3). fully supported on macOS. Source and changes: [creative-mcp/cli](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/tree/main/cli).

## Install and launch a server by hand

### One published app server

```
claude mcp add illustrator -- npx -y adobe-mcp-illustrator
```

Substitute the desired package name. For another MCP client, configure the command and arguments instead of running it as a one-shot shell command.

### Suite coordinator

```
claude mcp add adobe -- npx -y adobe-mcp-suite
```

Optional global install is documented for the suite package:

```
npm install -g adobe-mcp-suite
```

### Homebrew

The Creative MCP tap installs the Suite coordinator and links every app server, including the InDesign UXP bridge, onto your `PATH`. Homebrew 7 and later asks you to trust a third-party tap once.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
```

Installed commands: `adobe-mcp-suite`, `adobe-mcp-indesign`, `adobe-mcp-indesign-uxp-bridge`, `adobe-mcp-illustrator`, `adobe-mcp-photoshop`, `adobe-mcp-premiere` and `adobe-mcp-aftereffects`. Point your client at the command name instead of `npx`.

## Suite app selection

The coordinator accepts `--apps ids`, `--apps=ids`, or `ADOBE_MCP_APPS`. If none is supplied, it loads InDesign and Illustrator, the current workflow dependencies. Use `all` to load all five app servers.

```
npx -y adobe-mcp-suite --apps indesign,illustrator
npx -y adobe-mcp-suite --apps=photoshop,aftereffects
ADOBE_MCP_APPS=premiere npx -y adobe-mcp-suite
npx -y adobe-mcp-suite --apps all
```

Valid IDs: `indesign`, `illustrator`, `photoshop`, `aftereffects`, `premiere`. Unknown IDs fail startup. Loading an app does not add coordinator workflows for it.

## Run from a source checkout

```
git clone https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp.git
cd adobe-mcp
npm install

# Suite coordinator
node packages/suite/src/index.js --apps indesign,illustrator

# Standalone MCP server
node packages/illustrator/src/index.js
```

These entrypoints stay open and speak MCP over stdio, so a client should launch them. The repository’s root scripts are for development checks, not a separate product CLI:

```
npm run check
npm test
```

## No generic CLI command surface

For the app servers, the documented interface is the MCP protocol, not shell flags like `--help`, `status` or `export`. To inspect tools, connect the server and use `tools/list` or the server’s MCP `help` tool. To smoke-check startup, use an MCP client or send MCP initialization and tool-list requests over stdio; tests use stubs and do not require Adobe apps.

## Configuration variables

| Variable | Scope | Use

| `ADOBE_MCP_APPS` | Suite | Comma-separated app IDs; suite-only.

| `*_ALLOWED_DIRS` | App-specific | Additional file directories. Use colon-separated paths on macOS and semicolons on Windows.

| `*_APP_NAME` | Where package supports it | Select or identify the local Adobe app; see that package guide.

| `*_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS` | App-specific | Script/operation wait limit; defaults vary by package.

| `*_BACKEND`, `*_TARGET` | Supported packages only | Select documented backend or compatible local ArtCraft target.

| `PREMIERE_WS_PORT` | Premiere | Loopback bridge port; configure the same value in the plugin panel.

| `BRIDGE_TOKEN`, `PREMIERE_BRIDGE_TOKEN` | Premiere | Optional shared secret for local bridge authentication; keep private.

These patterns are not universal aliases: check the app README for exact accepted names, defaults, precedence and whether the Suite coordinator forwards them. Configure variables inside the MCP client’s server entry and restart the process after changes.

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / Architecture & distribution

How the series fits together

# Architecture & distribution

Creative MCP is a series of independent MCP implementations created by Zach Shallbetter. Each tool lives in its own repository and release cycle. They share one website, one Homebrew tap, one catalogue and one installer.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## The series today

Each implementation is a separate project with its own language, licence and release process. They share no runtime, API or process. A client can load several at once, but moving files between them is a handoff you manage.

| Project | Source | Language | Install | Licence

| [Adobe MCP](https://creativemcp.com/apps.html): five app servers, Suite coordinator, shared core | [adobe-mcp](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp) | Node.js 18+ | Homebrew `zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp` (v0.3.0), npm `adobe-mcp-suite` | MIT

| [Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html): Rust server, CLI and Blender add-on | [blender-mcp-rs](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs) | Rust | Homebrew `zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp` (v0.5.1), Cargo from source | MIT OR Apache-2.0

| Website, docs and series catalogue | [creative-mcp](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp) | HTML, Python, JSON | Served at creativemcp.com | MIT for code; content and brand reserved

| Homebrew tap | [homebrew-tap](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/homebrew-tap) | Ruby formulae | `brew tap zachshallbetter/tap` |

## How releases reach you

Every tool is published through its own ecosystem first (npm for Adobe MCP, Cargo for Blender MCP), then gets a formula in the Creative MCP Homebrew tap. Homebrew installs the runtime the tool needs, so you don't have to set up Node.js or Rust yourself.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap        # Homebrew 7+: trust a third-party tap once
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp
```

Each formula runs a real MCP `initialize` check as its test. Update with `brew upgrade`.

## One installer for the series

Status: Implemented and tested (v0.2.3). Fully supported on macOS. Linux detects apps only when their command is on `PATH`. Windows looks for the apps in their default install folders (not yet checked on a real Windows machine); anywhere, `creative-mcp add blender` sets up a tool without detection.

A browser can't see which apps you have installed, so the series has a small local installer that can.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp
creative-mcp setup
```

`creative-mcp setup`:

- detects installed creative apps (on macOS by bundle ID, for example `com.adobe.Photoshop` and `org.blenderfoundation.blender`, with their versions) and MCP clients (their command, including the Claude Code CLI bundled with Claude Desktop, or their config file)
- suggests the tools that match your apps and asks before choosing any
- reads what each client already has registered and leaves current entries alone, so running it again changes nothing
- shows every command it will run and every config entry it will write, and asks again before changing anything
- installs with Homebrew, or with npm or Cargo when Homebrew isn't available
- registers servers with Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through their own `mcp add` commands, and with Claude Desktop and Cursor by editing their JSON config. Each file is backed up once before the first change, and other settings are kept.
- only registers the servers your apps need. The Suite coordinator, for example, is offered only when both Illustrator and InDesign are installed.
- checks that each server answers MCP `initialize`, then tells you which clients to restart and gives a few requests to try

For everyday use it also has `doctor` (are the servers answering, are the running apps reachable, which clients have which servers, and the command that fixes each problem), `update`, `add <tool>`, `remove <tool>`, `detect` and `list`, plus `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--tools`, `--clients` and `--json`. The full reference is in [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html#installer). Detection runs only on your machine and sends nothing anywhere. Source: [creative-mcp/cli](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/tree/main/cli).

## One catalogue for every tool

Status: Draft. The first version of the catalogue is published at [creativemcp.com/registry.json](https://creativemcp.com/registry.json), with a [JSON Schema](https://creativemcp.com/registry.schema.json), and validated on every change in the [creative-mcp repository](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/tree/main/registry). The `creative-mcp` installer reads it. These pages are still written by hand.

The installer is built from this catalogue. Every other place that lists tools (these docs, the setup builder, [llms.txt](https://creativemcp.com/llms.txt) and the tap) will read it too. Each entry records the tool's repository, licence, author, capability status, install methods, server commands, the apps it targets and how to detect them, and the clients it supports. Adding a tool to the series then means adding one entry.

## Conventions for new tools

| Thing | Rule | Example

| Catalogue ID | Lowercase subject, one word | `adobe`, `blender`

| Repository | `<id>-mcp` | `adobe-mcp`

| Homebrew formula | `<id>-mcp` in `zachshallbetter/tap` | `blender-mcp`

| Packages and server commands | `<id>-mcp`, plus `<id>-mcp-<app>` for per-app servers | `adobe-mcp-photoshop`

| Client registration name | `<id>`, or `<app>` for a per-app server | `claude mcp add photoshop -- adobe-mcp-photoshop`

| Docs page | `/docs/implementations/<id>.html` | [Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)

| Capability status | Documented, Implemented, Tested or Validated | See [Content & capability guide](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)

## Adding a tool to the series

- Create the repository with a README, licence files, contribution guide and tagged releases.
- Publish a package and add a formula to the tap with a working test.
- Add the entry to [`registry/registry.json`](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/blob/main/registry/registry.json), with detection rules checked on a real machine (mark unchecked ones `"verified": false`).
- Add the implementation guide to these docs.
- Record capability status honestly: only Validated means the workflow ran in the real app and its result was checked.

See the [contribution guide](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html) for review expectations.

Source: https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / Contribute

Contributing · implementation by implementation

# Make a useful tool easier to reach.

Creative MCP is a collection of open implementations for creative applications. A contribution should make one implementation or a documented workflow more useful while keeping its capabilities and limits clear.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

Start with the project

## Choose the right home for the change.

### Adobe MCP

Adobe app servers and coordinator work live in the Adobe MCP repository. Follow that repository’s contributor instructions and app-specific requirements.
[Open Adobe MCP on GitHub ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp)

### Blender MCP

The Rust CLI, Blender companion add-on and Blender-specific documentation live in the Blender MCP repository. Follow its current build and contribution guidance.
[Open Blender MCP on GitHub ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs)

These implementations are maintained in separate repositories and have separate setup and capability boundaries. A shared website does not imply a shared runtime, API or automatic handoff.

Proposing a new tool

## Join the series with the same conventions.

A new implementation gets its own repository, published package, Homebrew formula in `zachshallbetter/tap`, implementation guide and, a catalogue entry with detection rules checked on a real machine. Names follow one pattern: `<id>-mcp` for the repository, formula and package, and `<id>-mcp-<app>` for per-app servers.
[Read the architecture & conventions →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html#adding-a-tool)

Site, docs and catalogue changes go to the public [creative-mcp repository](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp); see its [contribution guide](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Make the contribution reviewable

## Show what changed and how you know.

### State the user task.

Name the application, the operation, the required input and the expected result. Keep the change scoped to the relevant implementation.

### Keep claims tied to evidence.

Distinguish documented, implemented, automated-check tested and validated in the real application. Link the source or run record behind each claim.

### Document setup and limits.

Record supported application and client versions, permissions, platform differences, failure cases and any manual handoff still required.

For a workflow example

## Describe the handoff honestly.

When an example spans implementations, list which server performs each step, what the person exports or imports, what the client coordinates, and which operations have actually been validated. Do not imply automatic file transfer or cross-server orchestration unless the code provides it.
[Review workflow examples](https://creativemcp.com/workflows.html)

---

Source: https://creativemcp.com/apps.html

Beyond separate tools

## Carry creative decisions across apps.

The suite includes explicit cross-app workflows so source and destination apps can participate in a single task.

01

Place Illustrator artwork in InDesignPlace an artboard into a page as a link to the .ai file.
`Illustrator → InDesign`

02

Copy swatches into InDesignCarry exact color values from the Illustrator document.
`Illustrator → InDesign`

[Browse the full feature inventory →](https://creativemcp.com/features.html)

Install

## Every Adobe server in one install.

Homebrew installs the Suite coordinator and all five app servers onto your `PATH`. Prefer not to install anything? Each server also runs on demand with `npx`.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
```

[Build the setup for your client →](https://creativemcp.com/start.html)

Implementation guide · InDesign

# InDesign

The InDesign MCP server controls documents, pages and spreads, typography, tables, styles, images and links, long-document workflows, interactive output, prepress and export.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

documents; pages, spreads and parent pages; text, stories and tables; typography and styles; images, links and color; books, indexing and cross-references; data merge; prepress and export; preferences and scripting.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

ExtendScript via AppleScript on macOS or COM through PowerShell on Windows. Optional UXP bridge backends are described in the package guide.

Prerequisites

### What you need

InDesign 2023 or later recommended; Node.js 18+; macOS or Windows.

Package: `adobe-mcp-indesign`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

Use MCP help to inspect tools by category and exact arguments. A generated tool reference lives in the package docs. The package also includes optional UXP backend and bridge setup.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Measurements in the main tool set are commonly millimetres. Verify each tool description; object indices and units are tool-specific. File paths stay under the home folder plus INDESIGN_ALLOWED_DIRS.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`INDESIGN_APP_NAME, INDESIGN_BACKEND, INDESIGN_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS, INDESIGN_ALLOWED_DIRS, INDESIGN_TARGET; optional UXP bridge settings.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add indesign -- npx -y adobe-mcp-indesign
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## Full reference

The repository README is maintained alongside this implementation and covers exact setup, tool families, package-specific behavior, limitations, security and development status.

- [InDesign package README ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/blob/main/packages/indesign/README.md)
- [Generated InDesign tool reference ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/indesign/docs/TOOLS.md)
- [Browse package source and supporting docs ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/indesign)
- [MCP API conventions ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)
- [Launch and environment reference ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)

Implementation guide · Illustrator

# Illustrator

The Illustrator MCP server works with documents, artboards, layers, vector shapes and paths, text, color, appearance, effects, symbols, patterns, images, actions, variables and export.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

document setup; artboards; artwork, shapes, paths and transforms; layers and selection; text and styles; color and appearance; effects, blends, brushes, patterns and symbols; images and export; actions and prepress.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

ExtendScript via AppleScript on macOS or COM through PowerShell on Windows.

Prerequisites

### What you need

Illustrator 2023 or later; Node.js 18+; macOS or Windows.

Package: `adobe-mcp-illustrator`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

Use live MCP tools/list and help for exact definitions. Check coordinate direction, artboard index and target selector before editing.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Geometry uses points from the active artboard’s top-left; y increases downward. Target artwork by item ids, names or selection. Color accepts named swatches or documented color strings. File paths are home-folder confined plus ILLUSTRATOR_ALLOWED_DIRS.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`ILLUSTRATOR_APP_NAME, ILLUSTRATOR_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS, ILLUSTRATOR_ALLOWED_DIRS, ILLUSTRATOR_TARGET and documented shared backend settings.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add illustrator -- npx -y adobe-mcp-illustrator
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## Full reference

The repository README is maintained alongside this implementation and covers exact setup, tool families, package-specific behavior, limitations, security and development status.

- [Illustrator package README ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/blob/main/packages/illustrator/README.md)

# Photoshop

The Photoshop MCP server works with documents and formats, canvas and image data, layers and masks, selections and channels, adjustments, filters, painting and retouching, type, paths, actions, batch operations and export.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

documents and formats; canvas, image and color; layers, masks and smart objects; selections and channels; adjustment/fill layers; filters; brush and retouch; type and paths; timeline, actions and batch; export and print.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

ExtendScript through local desktop automation, with documented local ArtCraft adapter support for compatible tools.

Prerequisites

### What you need

Photoshop 2023 or later; Node.js 18+; macOS or Windows.

Package: `adobe-mcp-photoshop`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

The server includes a help tool. The package README describes tool families, units, target selection, timeout behavior and backend configuration.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Geometry is in pixels from the document’s top-left. Layer targets use IDs from list_layers, names or active:true. Supported color inputs vary by tool; review each schema. File access is home-folder confined plus PHOTOSHOP_ALLOWED_DIRS.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`PHOTOSHOP_APP_NAME, PHOTOSHOP_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS, PHOTOSHOP_ALLOWED_DIRS, PHOTOSHOP_BACKEND and PHOTOSHOP_TARGET; ArtCraft control settings where applicable.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add photoshop -- npx -y adobe-mcp-photoshop
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## Full reference

The repository README is maintained alongside this implementation and covers exact setup, tool families, package-specific behavior, limitations, security and development status.

# After Effects

The After Effects MCP server works with projects and footage, compositions and layers, time and keyframes, expressions, effects, text animators, masks, shape layers, paint/roto, 3D, tracking, color and the render queue.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

project and footage; compositions; layers and property paths; keyframes and animation; effects; text, shapes, masks and paint; tracking and 3D; render settings, output modules and queue management.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

ExtendScript through local desktop automation; Windows may use AfterFX.exe to run scripts. Compatible operations can route to EffectCraft.

Prerequisites

### What you need

After Effects 2023 or later; Node.js 18+; macOS or Windows.

Package: `adobe-mcp-aftereffects`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

Use help for the exact tool schema. Static script audit does not establish that operations have been validated in a live After Effects session; use the package README for current evidence status.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Use project item IDs or composition names as documented. Layer indices follow After Effects’ 1-based convention; time values are seconds where specified. File operations use home-folder confinement plus AFTEREFFECTS_ALLOWED_DIRS.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`AFTEREFFECTS_EXE (Windows), AFTEREFFECTS_ALLOWED_DIRS, AFTEREFFECTS_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS, AFTEREFFECTS_TARGET and EffectCraft control settings where configured.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add aftereffects -- npx -y adobe-mcp-aftereffects
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

Implementation guide · Premiere Pro

# Premiere Pro

The Premiere Pro MCP server works with projects and media, bins, sequences, timeline edits, markers, effects and keyframes, color, audio, graphics/captions, transcripts, metadata and export.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

Project and media; sequences/settings; timeline clips/tracks; markers; effects, transitions and keyframes; color and audio; graphics/captions/transcripts; metadata; export and application events.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

A local WebSocket server connects to the MCP Bridge UXP panel inside Premiere Pro. Premiere UXP initiates the connection to the local server.

Prerequisites

### What you need

Premiere Pro 25.6+; Node.js 18+; macOS or Windows; UXP Developer Tool to load the plugin until the package provides a published installation route.

Package: `adobe-mcp-premiere`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

The package guide says not yet tested against a real Premiere Pro session. Read its security, version-specific API limitations, connection steps and “What is not certain yet” section before production use.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Times are seconds. Clips use track and index values returned by list_clips; indexes shift after edits. Project item IDs come from list_project_items. Output paths must be home-folder or PREMIERE_ALLOWED_DIRS; overwrites require explicit option.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`PREMIERE_WS_PORT, BRIDGE_TOKEN or PREMIERE_BRIDGE_TOKEN, PREMIERE_ALLOWED_DIRS, PREMIERE_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS, PREMIERE_CONNECT_WAIT_MS.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add premiere -- npx -y adobe-mcp-premiere
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## Full reference

The repository README is maintained alongside this implementation and covers exact setup, tool families, package-specific behavior, limitations, security and development status.

- [Premiere Pro package README ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/blob/main/packages/premiere/README.md)
- [Browse package source and supporting docs ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/adobe-mcp/tree/main/packages/premiere)
