Implementation guide · Suite coordinator

# Suite coordinator

The Suite coordinator joins app servers behind two explicit cross-app workflows: placing Illustrator artwork in InDesign and copying supported Illustrator swatches into InDesign.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

Workflow: place an artboard from the active Illustrator document on an InDesign page as a linked .ai file; copy supported RGB/CMYK process, spot and gray swatches while preserving InDesign built-ins. Gradients and patterns are reported, not copied.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

Starts standalone MCP server implementations as local child processes and delegates workflow steps through MCP. It speaks MCP over stdio to the client.

Prerequisites

### What you need

Node.js 18+ and InDesign plus Illustrator for its current workflows. Other child apps can be selected, but that does not add coordinator workflows.

Package: `adobe-mcp-suite`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

The coordinator advertises its own workflow tools only; it does not mirror child tool inventories. Install standalone app servers for direct app tools. Use its package README for delegation semantics and constraints.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Select child app IDs with --apps or ADOBE_MCP_APPS. Current workflows need both InDesign and Illustrator. File permissions remain app-specific: configure both participating app servers as needed.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`ADOBE_MCP_APPS plus per-app variables documented by each child package; the coordinator forwards matching variables rather than acting as a single app backend.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add suite -- npx -y adobe-mcp-suite
```

With Homebrew, the coordinator and every app server are installed on your `PATH`:

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/adobe-mcp
claude mcp add suite -- adobe-mcp-suite
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## Full reference

The repository README is maintained alongside this implementation and covers exact setup, tool families, package-specific behavior, limitations, security and development status.

Implementation guide · Shared core

# Shared core

The shared core package provides infrastructure used by the Adobe app servers: safe argument normalization and script literals, path policy, script execution, structured results, MCP server construction, annotations and static script auditing.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

safe string/number/enum/path conversion; execution adapters; structured result parsing; failure detection; alias normalization; MCP tools/list and tools/call; annotation metadata; static API audits.

For feature-level detail and evidence, see the [Capability Atlas](https://creativemcp.com/capability-atlas.html).

## Connection and requirements

Runtime route

### How it reaches the app

A JavaScript library dependency, not a standalone MCP server and not a user-facing CLI.

Prerequisites

### What you need

Node.js 18+ when used by the packages. App runtimes are determined by the consuming server.

Package: `adobe-mcp-core`. Add it as a local stdio MCP server using [CLI & client configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

## API and content conventions

For contributors and integrators. The core README documents exports, executor options, error/result shape and tests. It does not provide Adobe app tools directly.

Discover the running package’s exact tool names and JSON input schemas through MCP `tools/list`. If the server provides `help`, use it to inspect a tool or category. Schemas from a different package version may not match.

Target and units: Core helpers are called by consuming packages; behavior such as application backend, paths and protocol is configured at the app-server layer.

## CLI and configuration

This package is launched as a persistent MCP process, not as a conventional one-shot CLI. Relevant settings documented by the package include:

`No standalone CLI configuration. Refer to each consuming package for environment variables and runtime behavior.`

Variable names and defaults are package-specific; consult the package README before changing them. File-operation permissions and bridge tokens should be configured in the client’s environment, not embedded in prompts or checked into source.

```
claude mcp add core -- npx -y adobe-mcp-core
```

For client-neutral JSON configuration and source-checkout commands, see [CLI & configuration](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html).

[Docs](https://creativemcp.com/docs/) / [Implementation guides](https://creativemcp.com/docs/#implementation-guides) / Blender MCP

Implementation guide · Blender MCP

# Blender MCP

A Rust MCP server and Blender companion add-on for scene and asset workflows. The server speaks MCP over stdio; a local IPC connection links it to Blender.

[Docs home](https://creativemcp.com/docs/)[Getting started](https://creativemcp.com/docs/getting-started.html)[Content](https://creativemcp.com/docs/content.html)[MCP API](https://creativemcp.com/docs/api.html)[CLI & config](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html)[Architecture](https://creativemcp.com/docs/architecture.html)[InDesign](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/indesign.html)[Illustrator](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/illustrator.html)[Photoshop](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/photoshop.html)[After Effects](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/aftereffects.html)[Premiere Pro](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/premiere.html)[Suite](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)[Shared core](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/core.html)[Blender MCP](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)[Contribute](https://creativemcp.com/docs/contributing.html)

## What this implementation covers

The project combines a Rust MCP server with a Blender add-on that performs scene operations. Its repository documents tools for scene data, geometry, asset workflows and Blender resources. For the current list of tools, parameters and behavior, use the [tool reference](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs/blob/main/docs/tools.md) maintained with the source.

The project is independent from Adobe MCP. They can be configured as separate servers in a compatible MCP client; direct Adobe-to-Blender handoff tools are not currently provided.

## Connection and requirements

Transport

### Local server and add-on

The client starts the MCP process over stdio. The companion add-on runs inside Blender and accepts the server’s local IPC connection.

Prerequisites

### Blender and Rust

Install Rust with rustup. Blender 4.0 or later is required, and the companion add-on must be installed and enabled (`blender-mcp addon install` does both).

Source package: `blender-mcp-cli` in the [blender-mcp-rs repository](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs).

## Install and configure

Install the CLI from the project’s Git repository:

```
cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs --package blender-mcp-cli
```

Or install with Homebrew. Homebrew builds the v0.5.1 release for you, so you don’t need Rust installed:

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/blender-mcp
blender-mcp addon install
```

`blender-mcp addon install` copies the companion add-on into each Blender version on your Mac and turns it on, so it loads and listens on `127.0.0.1:9876` whenever Blender opens. There is nothing to enable in Preferences. Quit Blender before running it; if Blender is open, the command leaves its preferences alone and tells you. The project CLI can add configuration for supported clients, including Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Antigravity:

```
blender-mcp client add codex
```

For client-specific scopes, add-on installation steps and exact options, follow the [current repository quick start](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs/blob/main/README.md).

## Safety and limitations

The add-on listens on loopback and is intended for local use; it does not authenticate local clients. The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python with Blender’s process permissions. Its pattern checks are not a security sandbox. Connect only trusted agents and review code before execution.

Scene-editing and file-writing tools can change or overwrite local work. Some asset search and import tools contact Poly Haven services; consult the project’s current README for the destinations and data involved.

## Full reference

- [Tool reference catalog ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs/blob/main/docs/tools.md)
- [Blender companion add-on guide ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs/blob/main/docs/addon.md)
- [Architecture and transport ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)
- [Source repository ↗](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/blender-mcp-rs)

### What stops a script

- BlocksAdding a colour with an existing name failsLook the colour up with itemByName and check isValid before adding; update the existing swatch instead.
- BlockscolorValue length and range must match the colour spaceSet space before colorValue and validate array length and ranges.
- BlocksClosing a document during a background export failsWait for the task (or use exportFile) before closing.
- BlocksIdle tasks can stop firingMonitor the task and recreate it; avoid relying on idle tasks for critical work.
- Blocks$.sleep blocks InDesignUse idle tasks or event listeners for deferred work.
- BlocksScripts run on the main thread one at a timeQueue jobs in the caller and use generous timeouts; split long work.
- Blocks'Object is invalid' after deletion or restructuringCheck isValid before use and re-fetch objects after structural changes.
- CorruptsRemoving items while iterating forwards skips itemsIterate backwards, or collect targets first with getElements() and then remove.
- BlocksBuilt-in PDF preset names are bracketed and localizedLook presets up and check isValid; fall back to iterating app.pdfExportPresets, or ship a custom preset with a known name.
- BlocksNamed presets must exist on the machineInstall presets with the script, or set app.pdfExportPreferences directly.

## How this was built

- Features come from Adobe's user guides and shortcut references; each record cites its source and is written in our own words. Third-party parity checklists were used only to spot omissions.
- Object models are generated from types-for-adobe (MIT), and for InDesign and Illustrator also from Gregor Fellenz's per-version references: InDesign 2023 to 2026, Illustrator 2022 to 2025, Photoshop 2015.5, After Effects 2026 and Premiere Pro 2024. No public object model exists yet for Illustrator 2026.
- Implemented and tested come from running every tool of adobe-mcp-indesign 2.4.0, adobe-mcp-illustrator 0.9.0, adobe-mcp-photoshop 0.1.0, adobe-mcp-aftereffects 0.1.0 and adobe-mcp-premiere 0.1.0 (all in the adobe-mcp repository) with the application stubbed, recording the calls each generated script makes and checking each script: ExtendScript against the application's object model, and Premiere Pro's UXP JavaScript against its UXP DOM. Nothing has been validated against a running application yet.
- Community scripts were parsed for the members and menu commands they use; no script was copied, and repositories without a licence are counted as evidence only.
- Menu commands are listed from published references and are unverified until run: Illustrator silently ignores a command string it does not know. Photoshop's Action Manager events come from Adobe's UXP event table, Adobe's bundled scripts and open-source helper libraries, and are unverified in the same way.

## Ready to try it?

On a Mac, one installer finds your creative apps and MCP clients, shows its plan, then installs, registers and checks every server.

```
brew tap zachshallbetter/tap
brew trust zachshallbetter/tap
brew install zachshallbetter/tap/creative-mcp
creative-mcp setup
```

[Every setup option →](https://creativemcp.com/start.html)[What the installer does →](https://creativemcp.com/docs/cli.html#installer)

Examples · real handoffs, honest boundaries

# Creative work, carried forward.

Explore concrete ways to use the tools together. Adobe MCP currently automates two Illustrator-to-InDesign workflows. Blender MCP provides its own Blender tools. Other transitions below are human-managed handoffs unless an implementation explicitly supports them.

Adobe MCP · supported workflows

## Two useful transitions, end to end.

The Adobe coordinator exposes these cross-app actions. It does not claim to connect every Adobe app or send files to Blender automatically.

01

Illustrator → InDesign

### Place artwork in a layout.

Place an Illustrator artboard into an InDesign page as a link to the source `.ai` file. Keep the editable source in Illustrator and arrange the placed artwork in the publication.
[Read the coordinator guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)

02

Illustrator → InDesign

### Carry exact swatches across.

Copy supported swatch values from the Illustrator document into InDesign, keeping the color decisions consistent across the artwork and page layout.
[Read the coordinator guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/suite.html)

Creative MCP · independent implementations

## Build a bridge when the tools differ.

These examples pair the independently installed Adobe MCP and Blender MCP projects. Export, import and transfer steps are explicit manual actions; the projects do not share an automatic orchestration layer today.

03

Blender MCP · local scene tools

### Inspect a scene before changing it.

Connect Blender MCP to a supported client, ask for scene information with `get_scene_info`, then use Blender’s own interface or MCP tools for the next edit.
[Read the Blender guide ↗](https://creativemcp.com/docs/implementations/blender.html)

04

Human-managed handoff

### Take a layout idea into 3D.

Prepare a graphic in Illustrator or InDesign, export an asset in the format you need, then import it into Blender yourself. Ask Blender MCP to inspect the scene or help with supported operations. File movement and app-to-app coordination remain yours.
[Use the starter brief ↗](https://creativemcp.com/downloads/creative-mcp-starter.zip)

Keep the boundary clear. The browser site does not inspect your computer, open creative applications or transmit local files. MCP servers run locally through the client you configure.

Make your own

## Start with a brief, not a promise.

The starter pack includes a creative brief and reference board for a small layout-to-3D exercise. It leaves the export format, transfer and Blender setup to your chosen workflow.
[Download the starter pack](https://creativemcp.com/downloads/creative-mcp-starter.zip)

Privacy · updated 3 November 2026

# What this site measures.

creativemcp.com uses Google Analytics to learn which pages and setup paths help people. It has no accounts, forms or ads, and nothing you do with the local tools reaches this site.

## What is measured

The site uses Google Analytics 4 (property `G-JBJ1NMP96V`). It records:

- pages viewed, the page you came from, and standard browser details Google Analytics collects, such as device type, browser and approximate location;
- clicks on named links and buttons: which one, and where it leads;
- switching between light and dark themes;
- in the setup builder on [Get started](https://creativemcp.com/start.html): the implementation, client and install method you choose, copying the command, and finishing the readiness checklist;
- words typed into the documentation and feature searches, the number of results, and which result you open; feature filters you apply.

Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses. Reports keep data for 14 months. Visits from the site owner and from development previews are filtered out.

## What is stored in your browser

- Google Analytics sets first-party cookies named `_ga` and `_ga_JBJ1NMP96V` to tell visits apart.
- If you choose a theme, it is saved on your device as `adobe-mcp-theme` in local storage. It is never sent anywhere.

## What the site does not do

- The setup builder and checklist run in your browser. They cannot see your computer, installed apps or files.
- The MCP servers and the `creative-mcp` installer run on your own machine and send nothing to this site. The installer has no telemetry.
- Nothing is sold, and there is no advertising.

## Your choices

You can block Google Analytics with your browser’s tracking protection, a content blocker, or [Google’s opt-out add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout). Every page still works with analytics blocked, and with JavaScript off the content stays readable; the interactive tools point to their written equivalents.

Questions or requests: [open an issue](https://github.com/zachshallbetter/creative-mcp/issues) or contact [Zach Shallbetter](https://creativemcp.com/about.html).
